title: Traffic
objective: After this level you can explain how traffic lights and road design keep cars moving safely.
summary: Traffic lights make crossing roads take turns, and wire loops in the road detect waiting cars by induction. Roundabouts cut conflict points from 32 to 8 and injury crashes by 72-80%.

cards.headline: The world's first traffic light exploded.
cards.body: In December 1868, a signal went up outside Parliament in London: semaphore arms by day, red and green gas lamps by night, worked by a police constable. In January 1869, a gas leak made it explode, burning the constable. Traffic control has come a long way since.

cards.headline: Red, green, and never both
cards.body: The first electric traffic signal went up in Cleveland, Ohio, on August 5, 1914: red and green lights at the corner of Euclid Avenue and East 105th Street, switched by hand from a booth. Its key design rule was that conflicting signals were impossible, so crossing roads could never both get green. That's the job of every traffic light: making drivers take turns.

cards.headline: How the light knows you're waiting
cards.body: Near many traffic lights, a loop of wire is sawn into the road. It's the most common signal sensor. An electronics unit energizes the loop with a current that keeps changing, and Level 8 showed that a changing magnetic field induces current. Park over the loop, and currents flow in your car's metal, lowering the loop's inductance. The unit reads that as a car and calls for a green.

cards.fact: A roundabout cuts 32 conflict points to 8.
cards.context: A conflict point is anywhere two drivers' paths cross, merge or split. A standard four-way intersection has 32; a single-lane roundabout has 8, and it removes the most dangerous crashes, right-angle and left-turn head-on, since everyone circles the same way. When US intersections were converted to roundabouts, injury crashes fell by 72-80%.

questions.prompt: Where was the first electric traffic signal switched on, in 1914?
questions.explanation: On August 5, 1914, red and green electric lights went up at Euclid Avenue and East 105th Street in Cleveland.

questions.prompt: Why are single-lane roundabouts safer than ordinary four-way intersections?

options.label: Fewer conflict points and no right-angle crashes
Cars can drive through them faster
Pedestrians are not allowed near them

questions.explanation: Conflict points drop from 32 to 8, and right-angle and head-on crashes disappear, so injury crashes fall sharply.

questions.prompt: A road loop senses your car because currents flow in the car's metal. Which Level 8 idea makes that happen?

options.label: Like magnetic poles repel each other
options.rationale: Poles repelling spins motors; this is induction.

options.label: Batteries store chemical energy
options.rationale: No battery is involved in the sensing.

options.label: A changing magnetic field induces current

questions.explanation: The loop's changing magnetic field induces currents in the car's metal, which lowers the loop's inductance: electromagnetic induction.
